title: The Call of Cthulhu by H. P. Lovecraft

cognitive_validation.rationale: The account is systematic, immanent, and explicitly nonsupernatural in framing: the beings 'came to the young world out of the sky,' are made of a shape that is not ordinary matter, obey a determinate stellar/cosmic cycle, communicate via transmitted thought, and are investigated through empirical inquiry (dream surveys, comparative ritual philology, geology, mineralogy). The story develops a coherent imaginary science of materialist cosmic horror; scientific method is a persistent structuring device.

novum_candidates.description: The Great Old Ones, chiefly Cthulhu: vast extraterrestrial beings who came from the stars in remote prehuman eons, lie in death-like suspension in the sunken city R'lyeh, communicate with sensitive humans through molded dreams, and await a cosmic-cyclical resurrection when 'the stars are right' that will overturn human civilization.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: Estrangement operates through the contrast between the reader's anthropocentric, rationalist empirical norm and the corroborated revelation of prehuman cosmic masters. The non-Euclidean architecture perceived identically by an educated sculptor and an unlettered seaman, the geologically impossible stone, and the globally synchronized cult rituals present the strange as objectively real, poisoning the narrator's perception of ordinary skies and flowers.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Old Ones govern the entire narrative logic. The framing (correlating dissociated knowledge into terrifying reality), the three-part investigative structure (bas-relief, Legrasse's cult, Johansen's voyage), the accidental awakening of Cthulhu, and the closing projection of humanity's doom all derive from and serve this novum. It is not an incidental device but the determining premise.

novelty.rationale: The Old Ones constitute a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: prehuman star-born entities who ruled earth, whose existence and looming return relegate humanity to a 'transient incident' and reveal the cosmos as fundamentally other than the reader's world. The corroborated identity of rituals across Greenland, Louisiana, and China establishes this as a world-scale reality rather than a local marvel.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The abnormal geometry is framed with an imaginary-scientific vocabulary (non-Euclidean, spheres and dimensions apart from ours) and corroborated by independent observers, giving it a coherent, immanent, nonsupernatural presentation rather than mere magic.

novum_candidates.description: The sunken city of R'lyeh, whose non-Euclidean, dimension-warping geometry defies ordinary spatial law (angles that read as concave then convex, an acute angle that behaves as obtuse and swallows a man).
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The impossible geometry creates strong reader-facing contrast with everyday space, reinforced by convergent testimony from disparate witnesses, but functions as a symptom of the deeper novum rather than the governing difference.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: R'lyeh's geometry is a vivid attribute of the setting and a subordinate estrangement device, but it does not itself determine the overriding narrative logic; it is an expression of the Old Ones/Cthulhu novum, which drives the plot's cause and consequence. The awakening of Cthulhu, not the geometry per se, governs the story's outcome.

novelty.rationale: A locale whose geometry belongs to 'spheres and dimensions apart from ours' is a genuine departure from the empirical spatial norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The idol's alien material is subjected to expert geological and mineralogical scrutiny, giving it a coherent empirical/cognitive framing.

novum_candidates.description: The carven idols/statuettes of a greenish-black stone that matches nothing in geology or mineralogy, said to have been brought from the stars.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The stone that no geologist can place estranges the reader from the familiar mineral world, but chiefly operates as evidentiary support for the dominant novum rather than as an independently governing difference.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The idols are recurring clues that link the investigations but do not determine the narrative logic; they point toward and serve the Cthulhu/Old Ones novum. They are an incidental (if evocative) device.

novelty.rationale: An unearthly material unknown to science is a novelty, but as an isolated artifact it is a token/evidence of the larger novum rather than a world-altering difference in its own right.
